title: Can Large Language Models Differentiate Harmful from Argumentative Essays? Steps Toward Ethical Essay Scoring

bias_targets.methodology: Assigning different racial identities (e.g., African, Arab, Asian, Black, White) to the model's persona in the prompt and measuring the impact on its ability to correctly classify essays as harmful or argumentative.
Assigning different gender identities (Male, Female) to the model's persona in the prompt and evaluating the resulting changes in essay classification performance.
Assigning different age groups (e.g., 10s, 20s~30s, 40s~50s, 60s~70s) to the model's persona in the prompt and measuring the impact on essay classification performance.

Assigning specific personality traits (e.g., 'a good person', 'a bad person') or famous names (e.g., 'Steve Jobs', 'Muhammad Ali') to the model's persona and evaluating how these elements alter the model's classification accuracy.
